docstring_dead_interpreter.replace:
Gemini CLI differs by release, measured on its hook runner with no model (results/hook-fidelity/gemini-core, 25
    releases of gemini-cli-core): from 0.30.0 on the call is DENIED, because the runner takes the error text as a block
    reason; on 0.29.7 and earlier it is allowed with a warning. The Gemini documentation says other exit codes only warn,
    so it is wrong for 0.30.0 and later. The measurement is of the runner, not of the whole CLI, and bash only.
docstring_dead_interpreter.with:
Gemini CLI differs by release. Measured on the CLI itself against a local stub model (results/hook-fidelity/gemini/sweep, 26
    releases from 0.24.5 to 0.66.0, 2 of 2 runs each) and on its hook runner (results/hook-fidelity/gemini-core, 25 releases of
    gemini-cli-core): through 0.29.7 the call runs with a warning; from 0.30.0 on it is DENIED, because the runner takes the
    error text as a block reason (the runner file changed in 0.30.0-preview.0). A hook that dies without printing anything is
    allowed on every release. The Gemini documentation says other exit codes only warn, so it is wrong from 0.30.0. Before
    0.26.0 hooks are off unless `hooks.enabled` is true. The measurement is bash on macOS; Windows runs hooks under PowerShell
    and is unmeasured.

gemini_ask.headless_warn_replace: --gemini-ask is on: interactive sessions get a prompt, but a headless run (gemini -p) waits for an answer that never comes
gemini_ask.headless_warn_with: --gemini-ask is on: interactive sessions get a prompt. A headless run (gemini -p) under --approval-mode yolo waits for an answer that never comes (hung 3/3 on 0.66.0 for shell and for an untrusted MCP tool, 2/2 on every release from 0.38.0 to 0.66.0 run, killed at the cap). Under the default approval mode a headless run is not asked at all: the shell tool and untrusted MCP tools are not offered to the model, and a trusted MCP tool runs.
gemini_ask.new_check_trusted_mcp: Add a warning when any mcpServers entry in the merged Gemini settings has trust: true: a hook's ask is dropped for that server's tools in every release probed (consumer probe: 11 releases 0.36.0 to 0.67.0-preview.0 in default and yolo, interactive and headless; stub runs: RAN 3/3 on 0.66.0 in both approval modes), so --gemini-ask cannot guard them. Suggested text: 'mcpServers.<name>.trust is true: Gemini CLI approves a hook ask for this server's tools without asking, so --gemini-ask does not guard them; a deny still blocks'. The in-session 'always allow' allowlist drops it too, settings-level mcp.allowed does not.
